reviewers.summary: The analysis is an unbound exploratory linear regression on a local dataset. Critical methodological and reporting gaps prevent any claim beyond data exploration. The study design is absent, variable definitions missing, no confounding control, no pre-specified plan, and p-values are inappropriately reported as 0.0000. The resultPosture explicitly deems this exploratory and not paper-ready.

findings.title: Analysis is unbound exploratory run, not a designed study
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md lacks any study protocol or analysis plan
findings.whyItMatters: The result cannot support the manuscript's implied inferential intent. Publishing exploratory output as a study misleads readers about the evidence level.
findings.actionableFix: Design a proper observational study with a pre-specified protocol, define the research question, and bind the analysis to a method-selection artifact before rerunning.

findings.title: No cohort construction details provided
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md 'Cohort Construction' section only states sample size, no inclusion/exclusion criteria
findings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot assess selection bias or generalizability. The cohort may be highly selective, making associations non-generalizable.
findings.actionableFix: Define the source population, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and any matching or restriction explicitly in the manuscript.
findings.deterministicVerification: No mention of eligibility criteria in manuscript.md

findings.title: Exposure and covariate definitions missing
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md 'Variables' section states details are in companion artifacts, but none are provided defining 'severity' or 'treatment'
findings.whyItMatters: Without knowing if severity is ordinal, categorical, or continuous, and how treatment is coded, the regression coefficients are uninterpretable.
findings.actionableFix: Define each variable, including its scale and coding (e.g., severity: 1-10 scale; treatment: 0=placebo, 1=active).
findings.deterministicVerification: Searching manuscript.md for 'severity' finds no definition; companion variables artifact not provided.

findings.title: No confounding control rationale; minimal covariate adjustment
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md only adjusts for age and treatment; no DAG or causal framework
findings.whyItMatters: The phrase 'after adjustment' is meaningless without a defensible confounder selection strategy. Omitted confounders can bias the severity-outcome association.
findings.actionableFix: Develop a directed acyclic graph (DAG) to identify minimal sufficient adjustment set or state the study as unadjusted descriptive.
findings.deterministicVerification: No DAG or confounder discussion in any artifact.

findings.title: P-values reported as 0.0000 (impossible exact zero)
findings.whyItMatters: This misrepresents the precision of the p-value calculation and violates reporting standards (e.g., report <0.001 or exact value).
findings.actionableFix: Report p-values with appropriate precision or as '<0.001'. Use exact values from stats-run.json (e.g., const p=3.98e-28).

findings.title: Model assumption checks incomplete and not reported
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md 'Limitations' states no explicit influence diagnostic evidence found, but diagnostics.json provides max Cook's distance; residual plot exists but not described
manuscript.md contains no assessment of linearity or homoscedasticity
findings.whyItMatters: Linear regression validity relies on assumptions. Without checking linearity and homoscedasticity, the standard errors and p-values may be invalid.
findings.actionableFix: Report residual vs fitted plot, Q-Q plot, scale-location plot, and assess whether assumptions are met. Interpret diagnostic thresholds.
findings.deterministicVerification: No mention of 'residual vs fitted' or 'homoscedasticity' in manuscript.md.

findings.title: Missing data handling not described
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md mentions 'complete-case exclusion' in Limitations but original sample size and missingness pattern unknown
findings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can bias estimates if missingness is not MCAR. Reader cannot assess risk of bias.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number of missing records, compare complete vs incomplete cases on baseline characteristics, and consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation).
findings.deterministicVerification: No missing-data table or description in artifacts.

findings.title: Influence diagnostics available but not discussed
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md claims 'No explicit influence diagnostic evidence was found'
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript contradicts the data. Even if below typical threshold (0.5), it should be acknowledged.
findings.actionableFix: Mention the maximum Cook's distance and state it is not concerning, or investigate points with higher influence.
findings.deterministicVerification: diagnostics.json.max_cooks_distance != null and manuscript.md states no evidence found.

missingEvidence: Variable dictionary with definitions and coding
Original sample size before complete-case exclusion
Model diagnostic plots (residuals vs fitted, Q-Q)
Clinical interpretability of effect sizes (severity scale units)

reviewers.summary: The study has fundamental flaws: variables are undefined, the data source is not described, and the analysis plan lacks pre-registration. Without variable definitions, the results are uninterpretable and irreproducible. Additional methodological gaps (missingness handling, limited diagnostics) further undermine trust. The manuscript's self-limiting stance does not mitigate these core deficiencies.

findings.title: No variable definitions or data dictionary
findings.whyItMatters: Without definitions (units, coding, meaning) of outcome_cont, severity, age, treatment, the reported estimates are meaningless and cannot be interpreted or reproduced.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a detailed data dictionary that defines each variable, its type (continuous, binary, categorical), possible values, units, and how it was measured. Include this in the manuscript or a companion artifact.

findings.title: Data source and ethical compliance not documented
findings.whyItMatters: The dataset is unnamed and lacks any ethics approval statement. This makes the study unreproducible and raises concerns about participant consent and data provenance.
findings.actionableFix: Describe the data source, ethics approval, and any data-sharing constraints. If the data cannot be shared, state this clearly and provide a minimal synthetic dataset that preserves the statistical properties for reproducibility checks.

findings.title: Complete-case analysis without accounting for missing data
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript mentions a complete-case sample of 240 but does not report the original sample size, number of missing values per variable, or any pattern of missingness. This can bias estimates if missingness is related to outcome or covariates.
findings.actionableFix: Report missingness patterns, consider multiple imputation or sensitivity analyses, and justify why complete-case analysis is adequate. At minimum, provide a table of missingness per variable.

findings.title: Insufficient diagnostic checks for linear regression assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: Only Shapiro–Wilk and leverage are reported. Homoscedasticity, linearity, and influence diagnostics are absent. For example, Breusch–Pagan test for heteroscedasticity and residual-vs-fitted plots are needed to support inference.
findings.actionableFix: Add and report heteroscedasticity tests, residual plots, and influence measures (e.g., DFBETAS). Include these in the diagnostics artifact.

findings.title: Causal interpretation despite exploratory posture
findings.whyItMatters: The objective 'How is severity associated with the continuous outcome after adjustment?' implies a causal relationship, yet the analysis is unadjusted for confounders (no covariate justification) and the run is declared exploratory. The manuscript's caveats do not fully retract the implication.
findings.actionableFix: Either reframe the question as purely associational without causal language, or, if causal, specify a DAG, adjust for confounders, and conduct sensitivity analyses. Clearly state that the current analysis does not support causal claims.

findings.title: p-values reported as 0.0000
findings.whyItMatters: Statistically, p-values are never exactly zero. Reporting them as 0.0000 is inaccurate and may mislead readers about the strength of evidence. The underlying p-values are extremely small but not zero.
findings.actionableFix: Report p-values using standard conventions (e.g., p < 0.001) or with full precision (e.g., 1.97e-30).

findings.title: No contextualization with prior work
findings.whyItMatters: The discussion lacks any reference to previous studies on the association between severity and the outcome. This omission makes it impossible to judge whether the estimates are plausible or novel.
findings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review to situate the findings and discuss consistency with prior results.

missingEvidence: Data source description and ethics approval
Missing data pattern and handling justification
Data availability statement or synthetic data for reproducibility
Pre-registration or analysis protocol for covariate selection

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
